profile.name: Jake Kim
profile.headline: I build cutting-edge financial software.
intro: An AI-native product engineer who started in crypto and has built dApps, on-chain games, and an institutional trading terminal.

Right now I'm building OrderX, a multi-exchange crypto derivatives terminal. I use Claude and Codex as planner and reviewer, run the systems I design all the way to production, and like building big products with small teams.

experiences.oneLiner: Multi-exchange crypto derivatives trading terminal. $10B notional processed and $1M revenue during pilot and private beta.
bullets: Cut steady-state browser memory from 3.8GB to about 1GB so traders can keep the terminal open all day without reloading.
Replaced react-grid-layout's CPU-bound layout math with an in-house translate-based grid, so chart-heavy dashboards drag and resize without stutter.

Established the team's AI workflow: context injection, a Claude–Codex planner/reviewer loop, and react-doctor cleanups to land the MVP feature flow. Built a Figma MCP + i18n agent pipeline for localization.

detail.description: A trading terminal that puts options, futures, and spot across several exchanges on one screen. Piloted with a large multistrat fund; $10B notional processed and $1M in revenue during private beta. I led the frontend from initial setup and designed its 18 feature domains.
impact: $10B notional processed and $1M revenue during pilot and private beta. Pilot run with a large multistrat fund.
Steady-state browser memory from 3.8GB down to about 1GB, so an all-day trading session no longer needs reloads.
Grid engine replacement removed React re-renders during drag and resize; no UX degradation with many chart widgets on screen.
AI workflow adoption let a small team finish the entire MVP feature flow. Localization automated through a Figma to i18n-agent pipeline.

projects.title: Browser memory optimization (3.8GB → 1GB)
projects.problem: Real-time streams, widget state, TradingView iframes, and query caches accumulated until Chrome sat at 3.8GB, slowing the UI and eventually killing the tab.
approach: Split orderbook and position-table updates down to row and symbol granularity to remove redundant re-renders and allocations.
Replaced AG Grid with an in-house DataTable with row memoization, virtualization, and clean unsubscribe paths.
Three-stage runtime recovery: partial resubscribe, then cache invalidation, then reload when returning from a background tab. Reloads are blocked while an order is being entered.

projects.title: Translate-based in-house grid system
projects.problem: react-grid-layout recalculated layout and re-rendered React on every mousemove during resize, saturating the CPU.
approach: dnd-kit plus imperative DOM transform (translate) updates so React is out of the loop while dragging.
Grid-to-pixel math isolated in pure functions and pinned with tests.
Widget stretch and shareable page layouts with auto-generated OG images.

projects.title: AI workflow adoption
projects.problem: A small team had to push MVP features across 18 domains at once, and AI output quality varied widely on a large codebase.
approach: Repository conventions, architecture, and domain rules fixed through context injection so any agent works to the same standard.
Claude as planner, Codex as reviewer: design, implementation, and review separated, with plan/design documents and gap analysis as the audit trail.
react-doctor cleanups run as a routine so debt from feature integration does not accumulate.

projects.title: Figma MCP + i18n agent pipeline
projects.problem: Design changes and translated copy were applied by hand, so every release shipped with omissions and mismatches.
approach: Figma MCP reads the design source directly to apply component changes.
An i18n agent finds missing keys, translates and registers them, and syncs with Lokalise. Localization runs on next-intl.

projects.title: Chart library migration (lightweight-charts → TradingView)
projects.problem: The backend speaks gRPC-over-HTTP plus WebSocket rather than UDF, so the stock datafeed did not fit.
approach: Provider-pattern custom Datafeed. Position and execution overlays, live quote push, per-account overlays.
Custom indicators (OI profile, visible-range profile, cross-exchange studies) and a range-preset toolbar.

projects.title: AI chat orders and multi-exchange widgets
approach: UIContext v2 RFC and an @account-tag routing proposal so chat orders can express batches, triggers, and TP/SL; negotiated with the backend team.
Spreader, Arb builder, Hedge simulation, RFQ, TWAP, One-tap buy. Documented the protocol limits of multi-account aggregation as a backend change request.

experiences.oneLiner: A roguelike minesweeper on the Abstract chain. Partnered with YGG Play and Raito.
bullets: The payment contract I designed processed 19,939 purchases with zero failures: 72,500 USDC, 25,000 USDT, 104.65 ETH, 50,616,446 YGG.
Upgradeable proxies let token-economy changes for repurchase and retention ship weekly without redeploying. Externally audited, live on mainnet.
Built and ran the client and in-game logic solo using context injection. Session keys record in-game actions on-chain without a signature each time.

detail.description: The Waifu Sweeper team under Yield Guild Games (YGG). Started as Princess Sweeper, later rebranded to Waifu Sweeper / Playpsweeper. I owned the entire web client and contract stack and shipped design changes (reward multipliers, season leaderboards, Gold Mine mode, revive mode) on a weekly cadence.
impact: 19,939 payments through the shop contract with zero failures: 72,500 USDC, 25,000 USDT, 104.65 ETH, 50,616,446 YGG.
Deployed to Abstract mainnet after an external audit (2025.12). 94 Hardhat tests cover purchases, the oracle, NFTs, and the session tracker.
Upgradeable proxies allowed token-economy changes (reward multipliers, season leaderboards, Gold Mine, revive mode) without redeploys, supporting repurchase and retention.
Owned the whole client and contract stack solo. Bot traffic blocked with Cloudflare Turnstile.

projects.title: Operating method: upgradeable proxies and context injection
projects.problem: The token economy (reward multipliers, repurchase incentives, seasonal events) changed weekly, and every touch of the payment contract put user funds at risk.
approach: ShopManager, NFT, and PriceFeed run behind UUPS proxies with a storage-layout review fixed into the deploy checklist. New capabilities such as the session tracker live in separate contracts rather than new proxy slots.
Game rules, entities, and reward logic specified through context injection so in-game logic changes ship quickly and consistently.
Result: 19,939 payments with no failures and weekly design releases.

projects.title: AGW session-key game sessions
projects.problem: Repeated actions such as opening tiles, defeating monsters, finding items, and reviving had to be recorded on-chain without a wallet signature every time.
approach: A hook that creates, stores, and restores a 24-hour session key with a fee limit and per-contract, per-selector call policies.
A WaifuGameSessionTracker contract that validates ordering with a per-player session id and action nonce.
Passed the tracker address as an argument instead of adding storage to the already-deployed ShopManager proxy, and documented why.

projects.title: NFT gacha and energy-pack shop
approach: ShopManager (UUPS): ETH/USDC/USDT/YGG payments with explicit per-token decimals, EIP-712 signature verification with nonce replay protection, slippage handling.
PriceFeed (UUPS): Pyth ETH/USD feed, confidence checks, cent-denominated pack pricing.
WaifuSweeperNFT (UUPS ERC721): batch minting up to 30, paginated tokensOfOwner to stay under gas limits.
Client: bundles Pyth price updates into the transaction, NFT as a payment method, YGG discounts.

projects.title: Live-ops tooling and seasons
approach: Season and Gold Mine leaderboards, reward dashboard, revive mode, referral-code validation.
Maintenance page with a service schedule, per-feature and date-based flags.
GA4 event design, Twitter Pixel, SEO/OG, BGM and sound effects, image preloading.
